label: Checkbox Group
title: Checkbox Group
summary: Use a Checkbox Group to let people pick any number of related options, such as accounts to link.
corePrinciple: Related choices, each independent, stacked with even spacing.

anatomy.title: A stack of Checkbox Items
anatomy.description: The group only spaces and themes its items. Each row is a public Checkbox Item with its own checkbox and label.

configuration.title: What goes in each row
configuration.description: The group accepts Checkbox Items only. Each row can be a plain label, a label with a link, or a label with an action on its end.

states.title: Selected, unselected, and disabled
states.description: Each row keeps its own state; the group does not limit or count selections. Disable a row only while the option is temporarily unavailable.
blocks: The checkbox dims but the label stays the same colour.

sizing.title: Full width, 12 px between rows
sizing.description: The group fills its container and adds no side padding, so the form around it sets the margins. Rows grow taller when an end action or a long label needs the space.

content.title: Make every option distinct
content.description: Start each label with what it is, then what tells it apart, such as the last four digits. Keep labels parallel and in sentence case.

inContext.title: Choose accounts to link
inContext.description: The screen supplies the heading, owns each item’s checked state, and enables the button once something is selected. The group itself only lays out the rows.

sources.title: Use the public Checkbox Group contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build) from the team’s private package repository. The group forwards modes to every item and end-slot child and uses a 12 px gap with no padding. Figma rows are 18 px tall; the installed rows render 19 px. On the web each row is one checkbox with one Tab stop that announces whether it is selected, and the rows sit in a list without list items; the group’s name comes only from accessibilityLabel. Row behaviour is covered in the Checkbox Item guide.
